Last Thursday (Nov 12), between 08:47 and 12:27 UTC, customer dashboards showed stale data for 3h40 [1]. The cause: ingest v2.14.0 (PR ingest#412) raised the default `max_batch_bytes` from 1 MB to 10 MB, and with the 512 Mi memory limit the ingest-worker pods ran out of memory on the first large batch and crash-looped — the change went to all pods at once [1]. The Sentry alert was the first signal, at 09:14, 27 minutes after the deploy, because there was no alert on consumer lag [1][10]. Rollback to v2.13.3 happened at 10:05 and lag fully drained at 12:27 [1].

No customer data was lost: events kept arriving in Kafka and were only processed late, confirmed by the Nov 13 reconciliation matching event counts per workspace against the Kafka offsets for 08:00–13:00 UTC [1][3]. Four customers contacted support (Orbitly, Zest Grocers, 2 trial accounts); Maya sent incident reports to Orbitly and Zest Grocers on Nov 15 [1][2].

What's changing, from the postmortem action items [1]:
- KES-431: page on-call when consumer lag exceeds 5 minutes (Noa, due Nov 20) [13]
- KES-432: ingest config changes go to the canary pool first (Daniel, due Nov 27)
- KES-433: raise worker memory limit to 1 Gi and load-test batch sizes (Lior, due Nov 27)

ingest#419 already reverted the default to 1 MB and added a memory guard that refuses a batch larger than 25% of the container memory limit [7]. Orbitly is also claiming an MSA service credit for this incident, which Sam is handling as part of the renewal conversation [2][6].
